mechanisms.behavior: Four balls rest on switches 18-21. Q1 ejects the rightmost ball through jam switch 22 toward shooter switch 23. The proven table pulses physical Tournament Start switch 15 as a software bookkeeping shortcut during release; never build a trough sensor at 15.
mechanisms.label: Four-ball trough

mechanisms.behavior: A ball at shooter switch 23 can be launched manually or by Q2. Preserve both the manual plunger path and ROM-driven auto launch.
mechanisms.label: Manual shooter with auto launch

mechanisms.behavior: The ball enters the Safe House saucer at switch 3 and Q3 ejects it. Q12 flips the building front down/open to expose the interior and returns it upright/closed when disabled. IPDB documents internal flashers and miniature army men; model moving collision geometry, not only animation.
mechanisms.label: Exploding Safe House facade and eject

mechanisms.behavior: Two independently hit drop targets report switches 11/13. Q13 mechanically resets both targets upright.
mechanisms.label: House two-bank drop targets

mechanisms.behavior: Four physical drive positions Q21/Q23/Q25/Q30 energize the 24 V stepper motor through cable 036-5634-11-A7; the proven script documents all four in its Q21 callback comment but uses Q21 alone as the logical VPX animation trigger. Their A/B/C/D electrical order is not established and must be derived when wiring the chosen motor driver. Switch 48 is active only at suitcase home; it clears during motion and returns near home. Q28 controls the separate lock/release post. The suitcase can lock three balls while open or closed. The proven table moves its facade through an approximately 358-to-320-to-358 range and its corrected visible-lock ordering maps bottom physical 43 to ROM 45, middle 44 to 44, and top 45 to 43; preserve that mapping and actual ball containment.
mechanisms.label: Motorized suitcase and three-ball visible lock

mechanisms.behavior: Q14 opens the Sniper House to reveal switch 62 and closes it to obscure the shot. Q29 raises or lowers the adjacent post. IPDB reports that the sniper figure waggles when firing; preserve the opening obstruction, revealed target, post collision, and figure motion.
mechanisms.label: Sniper House facade, target, and up-post

mechanisms.behavior: Single drop switches 60/61 latch down when hit; Q4/Q5 reset the left/right targets independently. Along with the Sniper area, these targets can obscure and free shots, so their collision state must follow the physical target position.
mechanisms.label: Left and right single drop targets

mechanisms.behavior: Q6/Q7 command the two route gates. Switch 14 senses the left gate/route contact used by the proven table; retain gate collision direction and sustained switch state rather than a cosmetic animation.
mechanisms.label: Left and right control gates

mechanisms.behavior: Q22 raises and lowers the left-ramp post. It has no public endpoint sensor, so the controller state is the command while the physical post collision must track travel.
mechanisms.label: Left-ramp up-post

mechanisms.behavior: Q15/Q16 drive the left/right flippers. Public button/EOS pairs are 84/83 and 82/81; both EOS contacts are normally closed.
mechanisms.label: Lower flippers

mechanisms.behavior: Left, right, and bottom pop pairs are Q9/SW30, Q10/SW31, and Q11/SW32.
mechanisms.label: Three pop bumpers

mechanisms.behavior: Left and right slingshot pairs are Q17/SW26 and Q18/SW27.
mechanisms.label: Lower slingshots

mechanisms.behavior: Q8 drives the optional 16 VAC shaker. ROM v1.44 added shaker code; absence remains a valid cabinet configuration.
mechanisms.label: Optional shaker motor

mechanisms.behavior: Switch 10 is the left-loop spinner; 46/54 are the left/right orbits; 58 is right-ramp entrance; 55-57 are top lanes; 24/25 and 29/28 are lower outlane/return pairs. The working table uses sustained Hit/UnHit state for route contacts and pulses spinner/fast triggers only.
mechanisms.label: Ramp, orbit, spinner, and lane network

mechanisms.behavior: Fixed contacts comprise the House pair 1/2, Cell Phone 4, CHLOE bank 5-9, MOLE bank 33/34, and right three-bank 39-41. They are pulse targets and have no reset actuator.
mechanisms.label: Fixed standup target groups

It explicitly shows Q17/Q18/Q22/Q29 on BRN high-side power, Q19/Q20/Q26-Q28/Q31/Q32 on ORG, Q24 on RED, and then skips Q21/Q23/Q25/Q30 before wrapping; the common SAM schematic maps BRN/ORG/RED supplies to J7-P1/J6-P10/J16-P4-8. High-side feed color is machine-harness evidence and need not follow the low-side Q control-connector bank.
